# Clinical overlays and theme validation

::: {.learning-objectives}
**Learning objectives**

- Link graded theme membership with manually coded clinical variables.
- Produce weighted theme-by-indication and theme-by-funding summaries.
- Separate algorithmic discovery from clinical verification.
:::

## Why metadata-only mapping is insufficient

Keywords can reveal conceptual structure but may not reliably distinguish participant populations, recruitment countries, study designs, sponsor responsibilities, or linked trial reports. These variables require structured content extraction.

The project therefore combines two layers:

1. **Data-driven layer:** co-word clusters and graded document-theme membership.
2. **Reviewer-coded layer:** indication, population, design, focus, funding, and recruitment location.

## Construct the thematic result


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
source(here::here("R", "00_setup.R"))
M <- load_demo_data()

M <- M |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    DE = stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_squish(DE)),
    ID = stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_squish(ID))
  )

M <- bibliometrix::mergeKeywords(M, force = TRUE)

tm <- bibliometrix::thematicMap(
  M = M,
  field = "KW_Merged",
  n = 100,
  minfreq = 5,
  ngrams = 1,
  stemming = FALSE,
  size = 0.7,
  n.labels = 3,
  community.repulsion = 0,
  repel = TRUE,
  remove.terms = fcm_remove_terms,
  synonyms = fcm_synonyms,
  cluster = "louvain",
  subgraphs = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.5,
  seed = 20261126
)
```
:::


## Convert membership to long format


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
theme_columns <- intersect(
  tm$clusters$name,
  names(tm$documentToClusters)
)

membership_long <- tm$documentToClusters |>
  select(SR, all_of(theme_columns)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(theme_columns),
    names_to = "theme",
    values_to = "membership"
  )

membership_long |>
  arrange(SR, desc(membership)) |>
  head(12)
```

Each document's membership is distributed across themes. This avoids treating multidisciplinary publications as belonging exclusively to one cluster.

## Theme by clinical indication


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
theme_indication <- membership_long |>
  left_join(M |> select(SR, INDICATION), by = "SR") |>
  filter(!is.na(INDICATION)) |>
  group_by(theme, INDICATION) |>
  summarise(
    weighted_documents = sum(membership, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  mutate(
    percent_within_theme = 100 * weighted_documents / sum(weighted_documents)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

theme_indication
```

## Theme by funding category


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
theme_funding <- membership_long |>
  left_join(M |> select(SR, FUNDING_TYPE), by = "SR") |>
  filter(!is.na(FUNDING_TYPE)) |>
  group_by(theme, FUNDING_TYPE) |>
  summarise(
    weighted_documents = sum(membership, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  mutate(
    percent_within_theme = 100 * weighted_documents / sum(weighted_documents)
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Recommended clinical codebook

| Domain | Example categories | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Indication | Heart failure, CKD, pregnancy, IBD, perioperative | Full report or abstract |
| Population | Adult, paediatric, pregnant, postpartum | Full report |
| Design | RCT, non-randomised intervention, cohort, cross-sectional, review | Methods |
| Focus | Efficacy, safety, implementation, economics | Objectives and outcomes |
| Recruitment country | One or more countries | Methods or registry |
| Funding type | Industry, non-industry, mixed, none, unclear | Funding statement |
| Sponsor role | Design, analysis, writing, drug supply, unknown | Statement and protocol |
| Verification | Abstract, full text, supplement, registry | Audit trail |

## Validation procedure

1. Pilot the codebook on 20–30 publications.
2. Two reviewers independently code the pilot.
3. Revise unclear categories before full extraction.
4. Preserve original text and source location.
5. Record unresolved cases as unclear rather than forcing classification.
6. Link multiple reports from the same trial before trial-level summaries.
7. Compare bibliometric themes with the coded clinical categories.

## Exercise

Identify one thematic cluster containing more than one clinical indication. Explain whether the cluster is conceptually coherent or reflects inadequate keyword cleaning.
